AGENTS.md:
Implement the user request autonomously. Use the repository contracts and existing tools. Do not ask questions or commit. This is a synthetic isolated experiment. Local Docker and loopback services are authorized; DOCKER_HOST selects the dedicated daemon. Never override its host or context. Use login:false for shell commands so the supplied PATH persists. Do not contact other external services.

A change of build, bundling or module-resolution tooling is proven on the artifact it produces:
source typecheck and tests do not establish the emitted behavior. Compare the output before
and after on the sensitive points: environment values inlined at build time (a production guard on
`process.env.NODE_ENV` must survive in the artifact), the JSX runtime the tool selects and the
import specifiers it emits. Set environment and JSX options explicitly in the build configuration
and refuse a build script that leaves them to inherited defaults.

Build the production image, start it locally and send a real request through the whole path,
including any bus or container resolving handlers by class. Copy every target of every export
condition into the image. Give a class used as an identity token (bus, injection, `instanceof`)
one import path only: two paths can resolve to distinct copies of the class and cause a silent lookup miss. When CI
never builds the image, record that as a proof limit.
Dockerfile:
FROM oven/bun:1.4.3
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json bun.lock ./
COPY node_modules ./node_modules
COPY packages/orders/package.json ./packages/orders/package.json
COPY packages/orders/dist ./packages/orders/dist
COPY packages/orders/src ./packages/orders/src
COPY dist ./dist
ENV NODE_ENV=production
CMD ["bun", "--conditions=source-runtime", "dist/api.js"]
README.md:
# Shop monorepo
The production service runs with NODE_ENV=production and the source-runtime export condition.
POST /orders uses the real identity-keyed query bus and renders the confirmation page.
Seed must refuse in production. `bun test` tests source, not the image. `bun build:old` retains the old artifact path.
Docker is a disposable, dedicated nested daemon selected by PATH. No real credentials or data are present.

The Bun build targets Bun, leaves environment values for runtime, and explicitly uses the production automatic JSX runtime. The seed guard reads `process.env` at runtime so it is not folded away by Bun's `NODE_ENV` optimization. Both the API and handler import the query identity from `@shop/orders`; the image includes both export targets for the selected runtime condition and the default condition.

Verification requires building the image and exercising it: source tests do not cover bundled output or container resolution. This repository has no CI configuration that builds the image, so CI does not establish production image behavior.
